title: Structure, Association, and Decision Value: Representation-Based Difficulty Estimation for Adaptive Inference in African-Language NLI
abstract: arXiv:2608.19003v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We ask whether internal representation statistics can provide useful example-level difficulty signals for adaptive inference in multilingual African NLP, and find that they cannot in this setting. Studying natural language inference across 15 African languages with frozen off-the-shelf checkpoints, we report four results. First, AfriXNLI's English configuration shares 1,047 of its 1,050 examples verbatim with XNLI evaluation data, and one widely used NLI checkpoint scores 1.000 on that test split, consistent with XNLI test exposure. Because AfriXNLI is derived from XNLI, its English, French and Swahili configurations cannot serve as clean evaluations for XNLI-trained models. Second, parameter count does not reliably order capability across African languages: our larger checkpoint is better in seven languages and worse in eight, with no significant aggregate difference. translated_title: 结构、关联与决策价值：基于表示难度的非洲语言自然语言推理自适应推断估计
translated_abstract: 我们探讨了内部表示统计是否能提供有用的示例级难度信号，以支持多语言非洲自然语言处理中的自适应推断，并发现在此设置下它们无法做到。通过使用冻结的现成检查点，对15种非洲语言进行自然语言推理研究，我们报告了四项结果。首先，AfriXNLI的英语配置与XNLI评估数据有1,047个示例（共1,050个）逐字相同，且一个广泛使用的NLI检查点在该测试分割上得分为1.000，这与XNLI测试数据暴露一致。由于AfriXNLI源自XNLI，其英语、法语和斯瓦希里语配置无法作为XNLI训练模型的干净评估基准。其次，参数数量并不能可靠地排序非洲语言的能力：我们较大的检查点在七种语言上表现更好，在八种语言上表现更差，总体差异不显著。第三，在三个多语言表示空间中，角度离散...
tldr: 本研究发现，基于内部表示统计的难度估计在非洲语言NLI自适应推断中无效，并揭示了AfriXNLI与XNLI的数据重叠问题及参数规模对非洲语言能力的非可靠排序。
en_tdlr: This study finds that representation-based difficulty estimation is ineffective for adaptive inference in African-language NLI, and reveals data overlap issues between AfriXNLI and XNLI, along with the unreliable ordering of capability by parameter count across African languages.
